subject: Opinion: We are suffering the consequences of the conservative revolution that began in the 1980s
posts:
A legacy of decay laid bare. Opinion: We are suffering the consequences of the conservative revolution that began in the 1980s.
Evidence: Market prosperity, systemic decay, private wealth hoarding.
#Aletheia #USPol #Economics

Proponents of the 1980s conservative revolution promised that deregulation, tax cuts, and supply-side economics would lift all boats, fostering widespread prosperity and robust public infrastructure.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +0.50) — Good Preference

Decades of data reveal a starkly different reality: crumbling infrastructure, soaring higher education debt, a hollowed-out middle class, and hyper-partisan media ecosystems born from deregulation.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.79, -0.66) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
The systemic shift prioritized short-term private extraction over long-term public stability, leading to structural decay.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 5.8, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Supply-Side Policy: FAIL (-0.79, -0.66) — Prioritized private wealth over public goods.
- Media Deregulation: FAIL (-0.82, -0.71) — Dismantled fairness rules for partisan profit.
The long-term consequences of the 1980s economic shift continue to shape modern American life, manifesting as deep wealth inequality and a severely degraded public infrastructure.

The Bright Side:
The visible failure of these legacy policies has sparked a renewed public demand for structural reinvestment, labor empowerment, and robust regulatory protections.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The Plane Error lies in confusing short-term market metrics (WHAT) with long-term societal health (WHO). The bait-and-switch promised universal prosperity but delivered concentrated private wealth at the expense of public stability.

Social Physics Analysis:
The 1980s reforms executed a Smart Selfish Maneuver. Under the pretext of "individual liberty" and "market efficiency," they systematically dismantled public protections, shifting the burden of debt and decay onto the working class.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between promised prosperity and actual systemic decay, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. This is the mathematical result of prioritizing private extraction over public health.

The Unavoidable Truth: Deregulating public assets without guardrails inevitably concentrates wealth and starves infrastructure.

The Unavoidable Lie: Cutting taxes for the ultra-wealthy automatically trickles down to benefit the working class.

Alethekanon:
The math of supply-side economics is structurally insolvent. You cannot starve the public square for forty years and expect a healthy democracy to survive on the crumbs.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see families carrying the heavy burden of educational debt and struggling with basic needs. We deserve a society that invests in our collective future and lifts up the vulnerable, rather than leaving them to navigate systemic decay alone.

Brothekanon:
Turns out trickling down was just a leak that never reached the floor. We traded solid roads and affordable college for billionaire space races. It's time to stop buying the hype and start fixing the actual foundation before the whole house slides.

Spirithekanon:
"For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind." Hosea 8:7 PASS
Deregulating public protections and cutting social safety nets for short-term private gain inevitably yields systemic collapse.
